first:
Create an ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET, not a character turnaround: exactly EIGHT consecutive frames of ONE complete in-place walking cycle of the SAME man, all facing the SAME direction and filmed from the exact fixed camera angle in the reference image. Use the attached ORIGINAL standing Ivan image as the sole visual identity and proportion reference. This is an image editing task: retain the reference character, clothes, normal adult proportions, camera elevation and painterly realistic rendering.

OUTPUT: transparent RGBA image, exactly 4 columns by 2 rows of equal rectangular cells, ideally 1536x1024 pixels (each cell 384x512). Reading order: top row frames 1,2,3,4, bottom row frames 5,6,7,8. Exactly one complete full-body character per cell. No text, numbers, borders, floor, cast shadow, background, props or extra people. Keep every boot, hair and backpack inside its own cell with generous margins. The head centre and pelvis centre must stay at the same relative position in all eight cells. Crown about y=24 and ground contact baseline about y=492 in each 512px-high cell.

LOCKED CHARACTER: young adult Ivan, clean-shaven, tousled brown hair, cream scarf, olive-brown belted Soviet surplus jacket, unchanged pockets/buttons/seams, small brown canvas backpack and straps, dark grey trousers tucked into dark worn leather boots. Match the original reference EXACTLY for head size, facial identity, neck length, shoulder width, torso thickness, hip width, limb thickness, jacket length and boots. Approximately seven to seven-and-a-half heads tall as in the reference, realistic adult, small natural hands. Do not enlarge the head or hands, make the torso stockier, shorten the legs, slim or fatten alternating frames. Same muted colours, even lighting, texture and exposure in all cells. No beard. No weapon. Do not redraw the costume as a different design.

LOCKED VIEW: the reference's three-quarter front view facing diagonally toward the viewer's right, slightly toward the viewer, slight top-down camera. Never turn the head or body to another direction, never mirror any frame. Walk IN PLACE toward the same lower-right diagonal on the implied ground plane, no translation across the cell, no running.

MOTION MUST BE A COMPLETE TWO-LEG WALK, not just stand and one repeated step. Describe the legs visually, not with ambiguous anatomical left/right:
The NEAR leg is the one attached to the image-left/near side of the pelvis in the reference. The FAR leg is attached to the image-right/far side. Their hips never swap. Each foot travels forward/back along the SAME heading of the man, not sideways. Knees track straight over toes, modest natural stride, no bow legs or sideways kicking. The feet are offset enough in depth that both boots can be understood.
Frames:
1. CONTACT: near leg reaches a modest step forward toward lower-right; far leg extends behind toward upper-left, heel lifting.
2. DOWN: near foot takes weight, near knee softly flexes; far foot leaves ground and starts to swing.
3. PASSING: near leg supports under pelvis, far knee passes forward beside it, far boot lifted a little. Feet do not merge.
4. UP: near heel lifts behind as weight rises slightly; far lower leg unfolds to prepare the opposite contact.
5. OPPOSITE CONTACT: far leg reaches forward toward lower-right, near leg trails toward upper-left. Opposite footfall to frame 1, NOT a mirrored drawing and NOT the same pose.
6. DOWN: far foot bears weight; near foot starts its swing.
7. PASSING: far leg supports under pelvis; near knee passes forward beside it, near boot lifted.
8. UP: far heel lifts, near lower leg unfolds toward frame 1's contact.

Subtle counter-swing of arms, opposite to the advancing leg. Quiet stable shoulders and head; slight natural pelvis motion only, never widening or stretching the body. Backpack remains the same volume and position. Render intermediate phases as genuinely distinct drawn poses, not repeated standing frames, not pasted/sliced legs, no motion blur or onion-skin duplication. The end of frame 8 must flow smoothly into frame 1. This will be cut into equal cells and played at 10fps: consistent registration and scale are crucial.

The attached original Ivan standing image is the ONLY identity/style/proportion reference. Exactly 8 full-body poses in a regular 4-column 2-row sheet, 1536x1024 ideally, equal 384x512 cells, top row 1-4, bottom row 5-8. Identical camera, head position, body width/height, pelvis and foot contact points in every cell. Feet remain firmly PLANTED in the same two spots of the original reference throughout. Crown around y25, boots around y490 within each cell. No walking, no leg changes, no body sway or pose substitutions. Only forearms and gun move, shoulder motion minimal. ONE CONSISTENT 1940s Soviet Mosin M44 bolt-action carbine: dark worn wood stock, steel barrel and bolt, short practical length, folded bayonet on side. It is the exact same weapon with the same barrel/stock shape and length in every cell, no gun morphing, no changing weapons, no disembodied hands. Both hands hold the weapon correctly; gunstock goes toward the shoulder, barrel points outward toward image right. The muzzle never points toward the face or crosses the torso. Keep entire gun and muzzle safely inside the cell.

Frames:
1. At ease holding carbine with BOTH HANDS across the lower torso, barrel angled modestly downward toward image right.
2. Forearms begin raising the same gun, stock approaching shoulder.
3. Stock contacts shoulder; barrel now almost level toward image right.
4. Aimed stance, stock seated, cheek close to stock, eyes aligned with sights; both hands correctly grip gun. Feet and body remain the original size and placement.
5. FIRE: exactly the aimed pose with tiny recoil toward shoulder and a SMALL muted amber muzzle flash at the muzzle tip only. No huge explosion, no body deformation. A single shot.
6. Recoil settles to the identical aimed pose, no flash.
7. Forearms lower gun halfway toward the relaxed carry.
8. Relaxed carry matching frame 1 so the loop closes.

Critical consistency: the gun must not change length, the body must not gain/lose weight, the face and jacket must not change between frames. Natural normal-size hands, recognizable original head/body silhouette. Sequential drawn animation poses, no blur or pasted/cut limbs. Keep the boots absolutely unchanged; this test evaluates upper-body and weapon motion.
